manifest.name: dsh-tui-favors
manifest.description: Fixed favorites for dsh-TUI: every launch starts on your pinned model, reasoning effort, agent preset and permission mode.
manifest.author: zerodegress

scripts.test: node --check index.js && node scripts/verify.mjs && node scripts/verify-host.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-tui-favors — one row that pins the four "favorites" a dsh-TUI launch
# starts on: model route, reasoning effort, agent preset and permission mode.
# With the opt-in `pin: true` (see below) it also protects every `/new`.
#
# Every key has a default in index.js, so `config:` may be empty. The row is
# composed by the dsh-tui profile; `apply` writes the preference files
# synchronously, so they are in place before dsh-TUI resolves its boot route.
#
# Configure the favorites in YOUR profile's cordis.patch.yml instead of here,
# so a local route stays out of the package:
#
#   - id: dsh-tui-favors
#     name: dsh-tui-favors
#     config:
#       provider: <provider>
#       model: <model-id>
#       effort: <tier>
#       preset: <preset-id>
#       permission: workspace-write
#
# ...or in `~/.dsh-tui/favors.json`: flat JSON with these very keys, which
# outranks this row knob by knob and is re-read on every `pin` check. It is
# validated by the same parsers; a bad value is reported and skipped, so the
# row's value stays instead of the knob going unpinned. `enabled: false` below
# is a kill switch — the file is then not read at all.
#
# Precedence (highest first) — what this plugin CANNOT outrank:
#   preset      DSH_TUI_PRESET  >  agent-preset.json
#   permission  DSH_PERMISSION_MODE  >  permission.json
#   effort      /settings 默认推理强度 (settings.json effortDefault) > effort.json
#   model       model.json is already the top layer (cordis.yml provider/model
#               is only the deployment default beneath it)
# `/favors` reports a note whenever one of those shadows a pinned value.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-tui-favors
      name: dsh-tui-favors
      config:
        # Master switch: false = write nothing, stay inert.
        enabled: true
        # Opt-in: keep restoring the files dsh-TUI rewrites when the user picks
        # another model/effort/preset/permission. `/new` re-reads those files,
        # so this is what makes the NEXT conversation go back to the favorites
        # too. false (default) = write once per boot; an in-session pick then
        # lasts until the next launch.
        pin: false
        # How often `pin` re-checks the four files (milliseconds, min 250).
        pollMs: 2000

readme.text: Pin the four values a dsh-TUI launch starts on — **model route, reasoning effort, agent preset and permission mode** — so every launch returns to your favorites instead of whatever the last session happened to end on. Turn on `pin: true` to extend that to every `/new` within the same run.

```
/plugin install github:zerodegress/dsh-tui-favors
```

Restart dsh-TUI afterwards: the row writes the preference files during startup.
Favorites come from two layers with the same shape: your profile's row config, and an optional `~/.dsh-tui/favors.json` that wins key by key.

Add your favorites to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (any knob you leave out is not touched):

```yaml
- id: dsh-tui-favors
  name: dsh-tui-favors
  config:
    provider: <provider>

Flat JSON, the same keys as the `config:` block above, sitting next to `model.json` and friends:

```json
{
  "provider": "magpie",
  "model": "group/cheap-deepseek-v4-1-flash",
  "effort": "max",

It applies without a restart when `pin: true` (each check re-reads it, 2 s by default); with the default `pin: false` a new or edited file is picked up on the next launch or by `/favors apply`. Knobs you leave out keep the row's value, and a value that fails validation is reported instead of applied — the row's value stays, so a typo never silently un-pins a knob. A whole copy-pasted patch row (with `id`/`name`/`config`) is refused with a hint to keep only the keys inside `config`. `enabled: false` on the profile row is a kill switch: the file is then not even read.

Then, inside the TUI:

- `/favors` — show each knob: the pinned value, its source (`[favors.json]` or `[profile row]`), what the preference file currently holds, and whether something outranks it (`DSH_TUI_PRESET`, `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE`, the `/settings` default effort). The `source:` line reports whether the file is missing, in effect, or ignored.
- `/favors apply` — re-read the file and rewrite the four files immediately instead of waiting for the next launch or `pin` check.

With `pin: false` (the default) the files are written once per launch: a mid-session `/model`, `/effort`, `/preset` or `/permission` pick stays in effect, and the next `/new` re-reads it — the favorites are back on the next launch. Set `pin: true` to revert those picks, which is what makes every `/new` start on the favorites; `pollMs` (2 s by default) then decides how quickly. It costs one `stat` per check and nothing else.

Two limits worth knowing: reasoning effort is pinned per launch (dsh-TUI caches the preferred tier in-process, so an in-session `/effort` lasts until the next start), and `permission.json` only seeds sessions that never picked a permission mode themselves.
